newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher, further gains expected.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher, further gains expected.

text.p: COMEX copper settled at its highest so far this year as the resilient market slowly mustered momentum to begin breaking through its trading range, dealers said.
July COMEX copper settled 1.50 cents firmer at 113.10 cents per pound, traded 113.40 to 112.00 cents. Spot May went out 1.60 cents firmer at 113.80 cents. Volume was estimated at 8,000 lots.

"This settlement is at the higher end of the trading range and the market is moving to new levels," Richard Hirsch of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said. "The reason we are going to go to new levels is that there is not much of a (LME) backwardation to attract stocks."
With a relative strength index (RSI) of just over 60 percent, copper futures were still far from being overbought, dealers said.
The LME cash to three months backwardation was $61/$65, staying within its recent range of $50 to $70.
LME stocks fell 1,750 tonnes Monday to 151,600 tonnes as the sharp hikes in stocks following a ballooning of the backwardation recently, evaporated.
The backwardation in the forward months on LME was attributed to some producer and option selling in very thin conditions, traders said.
Meanwhile wage talks at BHP Copper's San Manuel and Pinto Valley plants in Arizona start Tuesday when the United Steelworkers will ask for a "significant" pay hike, a union official said.

Workers at Phelps Dodge Corp's Chino copper mine in New Mexico, without contracts since June 30 1996, will protest outside the company's Phoenix head office Thursday, and the union filed three more charges against Phelps with the National Labor Relations Board last week.

Two power cuts in the last 24 hours caused by rain and high winds in northern Chile have created production problems, with El Abra facing a possible loss of 100 tonnes of cathode, an official at the plant said.
Chile's huge Chuquicamata mine's daily production was also cut Sunday by 10 to 15 percent because of bad weather, but monthly and quarterly output should not be affected, the company said Monday.
